name: DEMO, never a benchmark: the radial acceleration relation's one-parameter fit, replayed over its points (log10 g_bar, log10 g_obs and their 1-sigma uncertainties, one row per rotation-curve point), checked against what the paper publishes: g_dagger = 1.20 (within 0.10, a tolerance the replayer sets, not the paper), an rms scatter of 0.13 dex (within 0.02) and 2693 points. Every free choice the numbers depend on is a choice slot. The paper states the fitting procedure, the mass-to-light ratios and the selection; it does not state the fit's weights, so the weights are supplied, and the ledger says so. Engine 0.5.0.

sources.RAR-PAPER: McGaugh, Lelli & Schombert 2016, PRL 117, 201101, https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevLett.117.201101 (arXiv:1609.05917v1, PDF sha256 80357e5b689f1ae7c087359ff936a4543ad09bd4619498026d9e0bcf828fe8a8; LaTeX source PRL_RAR_arXiv.tex sha256 45ec63024e6a77b1c53ea92bf4305edf81bc069ebbd85a7d6da0eb897fbee9e2): g_dagger = 1.20 +- 0.02 (random) +- 0.24 (systematic) x 1e-10 m s^-2 (line 293); rms scatter 0.13 dex (line 304); 2693 points in 153 galaxies (line 38); the fit (lines 200-201), pinned in this build as rar.fit@1
sources.SPARC: Lelli, McGaugh & Schombert 2016, AJ 152, 157, https://doi.org/10.3847/0004-6256/152/6/157: the rotation curves and mass models (https://astroweb.case.edu/SPARC/Rotmod_LTG.zip, sha256 0a80cc90714828cc28b7dd57923576714d209f2490328c087c4a4ad607faf588; Table1 https://astroweb.case.edu/SPARC/SPARC_Lelli2016c.mrt, sha256 5aa0501f6b0d881fa579030e315e7b5b6ef561a5bd3a07472f9929c7e5728243)
sources.POINTS: the points as SCI-R1's preregistered script builds them from SPARC (r1_sparc.py, sha256 c332cce0b57823c663ea1996e7c3a3ff591c6bc630daf0d78c8ed597798fc63d, build_rows): the paper's 153-galaxy sample, errV/Vobs <= 0.10, mass-to-light 0.5 (disk) and 0.7 (bulge); sigma_y from the velocity, inclination and distance errors in quadrature; sigma_x = 0.11 dex times the stellar share of g_bar, floor 0.01 dex

default.source: RAR-PAPER lines 200-201 (orthogonal distance regression on the unbinned data, errors on both variables), as SCI-R1 read it; pinned in this build as rar.fit@1

choices.name: the fit's weights: "errors" takes each point's SIG_X and SIG_Y as its 1-sigma; "unweighted" gives every point sigma = 1

default.source: SCI-R1's preregistered weights, carried in the points' SIG_X and SIG_Y (POINTS). The paper says only that the fit "considers errors on both variables"; it states no weights, so these are the replayer's

choices.name: the disk mass-to-light ratio the points' g_bar is computed at (in POINTS, before the table reaches the engine)

default.source: POINTS: SCI-R1 computes g_bar at a disk mass-to-light ratio of 0.5

choices.name: the bulge mass-to-light ratio the points' g_bar is computed at (in POINTS)

default.source: POINTS: SCI-R1 computes g_bar at a bulge mass-to-light ratio of 0.7

choices.name: which galaxies and which points enter the fit (in POINTS)

default.value: 153 galaxies (inclination at least 30 degrees; asymmetric curves rejected); points with a velocity precision of 10% or better
default.source: POINTS: SCI-R1 applies the paper's cuts

LOG_GBAR.term: log10 g_bar, the baryonic acceleration (m s^-2) at the point [POINTS]

LOG_GOBS.term: log10 g_obs, the observed acceleration (m s^-2) at the point [POINTS]

SIG_X.term: the 1-sigma uncertainty of log10 g_bar, in dex [POINTS]

SIG_Y.term: the 1-sigma uncertainty of log10 g_obs, in dex [POINTS]
